real_qa.q: How did Arlington High School address social skill loss in students after COVID-19 school closures?
real_qa.r: Arlington High School implemented an intentional initiative focused on basic social skills. They started with teaching students simply to say hello, using a poster with three criteria: look people in the eye, use a pleasant voice, and say hello. Secret shoppers (about 12 staff members) stood in hallways with bingo dabbers during passing periods, marking students' hands when they greeted them back. Classes with the most marked hands won donut parties. This basic-level intervention worked well and helped students rebuild trust and connection.
real_qa.requete: Arlington High School COVID social skills initiative

real_qa.q: What is the counterbalance concept from The One Thing book and how does it differ from work-life balance?
real_qa.r: Counterbalance means accepting that you will never find perfect balance between work and life. Instead of trying to keep both at 50%, the concept suggests putting one at 100% during critical periods and the other at zero, then switching back. For example, during playoffs, a coach might work 15-hour days while the family accepts eating McDonald's every day, then after the playoffs end, the coach takes time off to focus fully on family. This eliminates guilt and helps people feel successful at both work and life.
real_qa.requete: counterbalance work-life balance The One Thing book

real_qa.q: What percentage of students wore hats and responded with anger to simple classroom commands after COVID-19 closures?
real_qa.r: About 50% of students who wore hats responded to the request to remove them in a way that was unlike their same-age peers, showing anger, shouting back, and having tantrums instead of the typical annoyed response. This aggressive reaction extended to other simple commands like turning in work, stopping talking, putting down pencils, and putting phones away. Teachers found that even when parents were contacted, they would also respond with anger and upset.
real_qa.requete: student behavioral responses COVID classroom commands

real_qa.q: Why did Arlington High School have 25% of staff absent on any given day during the return to full in-person school?
real_qa.r: A COVID surge occurred in January and February, with 25% of staff off campus on any given day. This made it extremely difficult to implement initiatives because from one day to the next, leadership had essentially 25% new staff, disrupting continuity and making planning ahead nearly impossible until February and March showed consistent staffing levels.

real_qa.q: What trauma and toxic stress training did Arlington High School leadership undertake to address post-COVID student behaviors?
real_qa.r: Stacey Humble realized after listening to podcasts over the summer that the issue was not just anxiety but trauma and toxic stress. She and her team took classes with Sylvia Fuentes on trauma and toxic stress, which helped them understand that everyone—students, teachers, the education system, and society—had gone through trauma during COVID. This reframing allowed the school to approach student behavioral challenges with an understanding of underlying trauma rather than just surface behaviors.
real_qa.requete: Sylvia Fuentes trauma toxic stress training education

real_qa.q: What percentage of students returned to Arlington High School in person at the beginning of the hybrid learning phase?
real_qa.r: When Arlington High School returned to a hybrid model with part virtual and part in-person learning, only about 25% of students came back to campus. This small number allowed the school to focus on helping these students turn in assignments and support them through the pandemic while many were experiencing sickness in their families and broader community.
